38776.e: In a list alliance, the votes of several lists are first added together. That way, fewer votes are lost, and smaller parties have a better chance of a seat.
38776.m: With a list alliance, parties add their votes together.

38777.q: Why is a calculation method needed to share out the National Council seats?
a: Because seats cannot be split into parts
Because the Federal Council wants it
Because the votes must be kept secret
Because there are too many candidates
38777.e: A party's votes rarely work out to an exact whole number of seats. A calculation method sets out how the seats are shared out fairly.
38777.m: A calculation method shares out whole seats as fairly as possible.

38778.q: Which parties does the Hagenbach-Bischoff method slightly favour?
38778.e: As with the D'Hondt method, big parties often get a small advantage with the remaining seats. That is why small parties often link their lists.
38778.m: The Hagenbach-Bischoff method slightly favours big parties.

38779.q: Why must big election campaigns disclose where their money comes from?
a: So that everyone can see who pays for them
So that they pay less tax
So that they may print more posters
So that the election goes faster
38779.e: Transparency rules have applied since the 2023 election. Voters should know who is behind a campaign.
38779.m: Big election campaigns must show where their money comes from.

38780.q: What is a donation to a party?
a: Money you give freely as a gift
38780.e: A donation is a voluntary gift. Parties must disclose large donations of 15,000 francs or more.
38780.m: A donation is a voluntary gift.

38781.q: What do parties often use to advertise along streets and squares during an election campaign?
38781.e: Before elections, posters with faces and slogans hang everywhere. Parties use them to draw attention to themselves.
38781.m: In election campaigns, parties advertise with posters.

38782.q: In which National Council elections did the new rules on transparency in political funding apply for the first time?
38782.e: The rules were a counter-proposal to the transparency initiative. They were first applied in the 2023 elections.
38782.m: Transparency rules for campaign money have applied since 2023.

38783.q: Which donations are banned for election campaigns in Switzerland?
a: Anonymous donations and donations from abroad
38783.e: Anonymous donations and donations from abroad may not be accepted. Donations from Swiss people living abroad are an exception.
38783.m: Anonymous and foreign donations are banned in election campaigns.

a: The time when parties try to win votes
An argument in the Federal Council
38784.e: Before an election, parties and candidates present their ideas. They hand out flyers, put up posters and take part in panel discussions.
38784.m: In an election campaign, parties try to win votes.

38785.q: What is the document called in which a party writes down its aims?
38785.e: The party programme says what a party stands for. That way, voters can compare the parties.
38785.m: A party's aims are in its party programme.

38786.q: Roughly how many voters took part in the National Council elections of 2019 and 2023?
38786.e: In 2019, 45.1 per cent voted, and in 2023 it was 46.6 per cent. That is just under half of those entitled to vote.
38786.m: Just under half of voters take part in National Council elections.

38787.q: How did turnout in the National Council elections change from 2019 to 2023?
38787.e: Turnout rose from 45.1 per cent to 46.6 per cent. That is an increase of 1.5 percentage points.

38788.q: In which canton is voting compulsory?
38788.e: Schaffhausen is the only canton that still has compulsory voting. That is why turnout there is usually much higher than in the rest of Switzerland.
38788.m: Voting is compulsory in the canton of Schaffhausen.

38789.q: How big is the fine if you do not vote in Schaffhausen without a good reason?
38789.e: Anyone in Schaffhausen who does not take part without an excuse pays a small fine of 6 francs. Even so, it works: many people vote because of it.
38789.m: In Schaffhausen, not voting costs six francs.

a: There were only a few parties
38790.e: Turnout shows how many people entitled to vote actually voted. If it is low, many did not go and vote.
38790.m: Low turnout means many people did not vote.

38791.q: A municipality has 4,000 voters, and 1,840 of them vote. What is the turnout?
38791.m: For turnout, you divide the number of people who voted by the number entitled to vote.

38792.q: Which age group in Switzerland usually votes least often?
38792.e: Election studies show that young adults vote less often than older people. Turnout usually rises with age.
38792.m: Young adults vote less often than older people.

38793.q: In which month does Appenzell Innerrhoden elect its member of the Council of States?
38793.e: Appenzell Innerrhoden elects its member of the Council of States at the Landsgemeinde (open-air assembly). This takes place in April, not on the national election Sunday.
38793.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden elects its member of the Council of States in April.

38794.q: In most cantons, what majority do you need to be elected to the Council of States in the first round?
38794.e: In the first round, you must get more than half of the votes that count. Anyone who misses this must go into a second round.
38794.m: In the first round of the Council of States election, you need an absolute majority.

38795.q: What happens if nobody reaches an absolute majority in the first round of the Council of States election?
a: The seat stays empty for four years
The Federal Council chooses the person
38795.e: Anyone who does not get more than half the votes in the first round is not elected. A second round then follows a few weeks later; in 2023, this was needed for 13 seats.
38795.m: Without an absolute majority, a second round is needed.

38797.q: Why is it hard for small parties to win a seat in the Council of States?
a: Each canton has only a few seats, so you need a great many votes
The Federal Council only elects big parties
The Council of States has no seats for parties
38797.e: Each canton usually has only two seats, given out by majority vote. That is why small parties rarely win; in 2023, for example, the Geneva MCG managed it for the first time.
38797.m: Small parties find it hard to get into the Council of States.

38798.q: By which electoral method is the Council of States elected in almost all cantons?
38798.e: In almost all cantons, whoever gets the most votes is elected. Only Neuchâtel and Jura elect the Council of States by proportional representation.
38798.m: The Council of States is elected by majority vote almost everywhere.

38799.q: Which law governs the Council of States election in the canton of Zurich?
a: The Zurich Act on Political Rights
The Federal Act on Political Rights
38799.e: The Federal Constitution leaves the Council of States election to the cantons. That is why cantonal law applies; in Zurich, it is the cantonal Act on Political Rights.
38799.m: The Council of States election follows cantonal law.

38800.q: Roughly what share of the vote did the SVP get in the 2023 National Council elections?
38800.e: The SVP got 27.9 per cent, a gain of 2.3 percentage points. It remained the party with the most voters.
38800.m: In 2023, the SVP had a share of the vote of almost 28 per cent.

38801.q: Which party was the second strongest in the 2023 National Council elections?
38801.e: The SP got around 18 per cent and remained the second strongest party behind the SVP.
38801.m: In 2023, the SP was the second strongest party.

38802.q: Does a party with slightly more votes always get more seats than a party with slightly fewer?
a: Only in the Council of States
Only if it is on the Federal Council
38802.e: Because the seats are shared out separately in each canton, there can be small differences. In 2023, the FDP had a slightly larger share of the vote than the Centre, but one seat fewer.
38802.m: A larger share of the vote does not always bring more seats.

38803.q: Which party lost the most share of the vote in 2023?
38803.e: The Greens fell from 13.2 to 9.8 per cent, a drop of 3.4 percentage points. After their success in 2019, they were the biggest losers.
38803.m: The Greens lost the most share of the vote in 2023.

38804.q: What does share of the vote mean?
a: The proportion of votes a party gets
38804.e: The share of the vote shows as a percentage how many of all the votes a party received.
38804.m: The share of the vote shows how many votes a party got.

38805.q: With which topic did the Greens win many extra National Council seats in 2019?
38805.e: In 2019, climate change was a big topic, and there were many climate protests. The Greens won 17 extra seats.
38805.m: In 2019, the Greens won many seats thanks to the climate issue.

38806.q: A party gets 18,000 out of 120,000 party votes. What is its share of the vote?
38806.m: You work out the share of the vote by dividing the party's votes by all the votes.

38807.q: How many seats does the National Council have in total?
38807.e: The National Council has 200 seats and the Council of States 46. Together, that makes 246 members of the Federal Assembly.

a: A polling station on the internet
38808.e: On Smartvote, you answer questions on political topics. The website compares your answers with those of the candidates and parties.
38808.m: Smartvote helps you find suitable candidates.

38809.e: Smartvote has existed since the 2003 parliamentary elections. Before elections, many people use the website to find suitable candidates.

38810.q: Why is it important for a voting aid like Smartvote to be independent?
a: So that no party is favoured
So that it only works in Bern
38810.e: Smartvote is run by the independent association Politools. A voting aid must not favour any party, otherwise it would not be fair.
38810.m: A good voting aid does not favour any party.

38811.q: What is the spider's web graphic called that Smartvote uses to show political profiles?
38811.e: The Smartspider shows on several axes how strongly someone supports, for example, environmental protection or an open foreign policy. That way, profiles can be compared easily.
38811.m: The Smartspider shows political profiles as a web.

38812.q: In the Smartspider, what does it mean when a point lies far out?
a: You strongly agree with this aim
You did not answer any questions
38812.e: The Smartspider has several axes, one for each topic. The further out a point lies, the more strongly you agree with that aim.
38812.m: Far out in the Smartspider means strong agreement.

38813.q: Who answers the questions for a candidate's profile on Smartvote?
38813.e: The candidates fill in the same questionnaire as the voters. Only then can the answers be compared directly.
38813.m: On Smartvote, the candidates answer for themselves.

38814.q: What is a well-known voting aid in Germany, similar to Smartvote, called?
38814.e: In Germany, the Wahl-O-Mat compares voters' positions with those of the parties. Smartvote also compares individual candidates.
38814.m: In Germany, the Wahl-O-Mat is a voting aid.

38815.q: Must you vote according to a Smartvote recommendation?
a: No, it is only a help
Yes, but only the first time
Only in Council of States elections
38815.e: Smartvote only shows who gave similar answers. Each person must decide for themselves.
38815.m: A voting aid gives hints, not obligations.

38816.q: What must you do on Smartvote to get a voting recommendation?
38816.e: You answer a few dozen questions on political topics. Then Smartvote compares your answers with those of the candidates.
38816.m: On Smartvote, you answer questions and get a recommendation.

38817.q: When is there an uncontested election?
a: When no more people stand than there are seats
When everyone has the same number of votes
38817.e: If there are no more candidates than seats, no vote is needed. All the candidates are then considered elected.
38817.m: There is an uncontested election when there is no choice between candidates.

38818.q: What happens to the candidates in an uncontested election?
a: They are considered elected without a vote
38818.e: If there are no more candidates than seats, no vote is needed. The responsible authority declares all the candidates elected.
38818.m: In an uncontested election, all candidates are elected without a vote.

38819.q: Is an uncontested election also allowed in National Council elections?
a: Yes, the federal law provides for it
Only in the canton of Bern
Only in the Council of States election
38819.e: Article 45 of the Federal Act on Political Rights also allows an uncontested election for the National Council. In practice, though, it rarely happens there.
38819.m: An uncontested election is possible for the National Council too.

38820.q: In a canton, one Council of States seat is free and only one person stands. What happens?
a: They are elected in an uncontested election
The election is cancelled and the seat stays empty
The Federal Council chooses someone else
The people still have to vote three times
38820.e: If there are no more candidates than seats, no vote is needed. The person is considered elected in an uncontested election.
38820.m: With only one candidate for one seat, there is an uncontested election.

38821.q: Where are uncontested elections especially common?
38821.e: In many municipalities, it is hard to find enough people for posts such as the municipal council or the school board. Then there are often no more candidates than seats.
38821.m: Uncontested elections are especially common in municipalities.

38822.q: What is often criticised about uncontested elections?
a: They cost a lot of money
38822.e: In an uncontested election, voters cannot vote anyone out or prefer another person. On the other hand, it saves effort and costs.
38822.m: In an uncontested election, the people have no choice.

38823.q: What can voters do to prevent an uncontested election?
a: Put in a blank ballot paper
38823.e: If more people stand than there are seats by the closing date, there must be a vote. That is why an extra candidate can prevent an uncontested election.
38823.m: An extra candidate leads to a real election.

38824.q: A municipal council has 5 seats and 7 people put their names forward. Is there an uncontested election?
38824.e: For an uncontested election, no more people may stand than there are seats. Because 7 is more than 5, the people must vote.
38824.m: If there are more candidates than seats, a real election takes place.

38825.q: What is an electoral list in the National Council election?
a: A list of candidates from a party or group
A list of the Federal Councillors
38825.e: Parties and groups put up lists of their candidates. In 2019, there were over 500 such lists.
38825.m: An electoral list has a party's candidates on it.

38826.q: Who takes over a seat in the National Council when a member resigns?
a: The next person on the same list
A member of the Federal Council
The oldest person in the canton
38826.e: The person on the same list who had the most votes but was not elected moves up. That way, the seat stays with the same list.
38826.m: When someone resigns, the next person on the list moves up.

38827.q: Where do Swiss people living abroad vote in National Council elections?
a: In their last municipality of residence or place of origin
In the federal city of Bern
38827.e: Their political home is their last municipality of residence in Switzerland or their place of citizenship. That is why their votes count in that canton.
38827.m: Swiss people abroad vote in the canton of their last municipality or their place of citizenship.

38828.q: What decides how many National Council seats a canton gets?
38828.e: The 200 seats are shared out among the cantons according to population. A big canton gets more seats.
38828.m: The distribution of seats is based on the cantons' population.

38830.q: May voters in Bern vote for candidates from the canton of Lucerne?
a: No, only for candidates in their own canton
Yes, but only for neighbouring cantons
38830.e: Each canton is its own constituency with its own lists. So you can only vote for candidates standing in your own canton.
38830.m: You only vote for candidates from your own constituency.

38831.q: How many of the 46 Council of States seats were decided on election Sunday in October 2023?
38831.e: All cantons except Appenzell Innerrhoden voted on the same day as for the National Council. Appenzell Innerrhoden votes at the Landsgemeinde (open-air assembly).
38831.m: Almost all cantons elect the Council of States together with the National Council.

38832.q: In the Council of States election in a canton with two seats, what is the maximum number of names you may write down?
38832.e: You may write down no more names than there are seats to fill. A canton with two seats has two lines.
38832.m: In the Council of States election, you write down no more names than there are seats.

38833.q: Why can't turnout in 1919 be compared directly with today?
a: Back then only men could vote
Back then there were no cantons
Back then people only voted in Bern
Back then votes were not counted
38833.e: Women only got the vote at federal level in 1971. So the voters of 1919 were a much smaller group.
38833.m: Until 1971, only men could vote at federal level.

38834.q: Which occupational group especially shaped the SVP when it began?
38834.e: The SVP was formed in 1971 mainly from the Farmers, Traders and Citizens' Party. Its green colour still recalls these roots today.
38834.m: The SVP has its roots in a farmers' party.

38835.q: Which colour dominates the SVP's logo and posters?
38835.e: The SVP uses a green logo that recalls its roots as a farmers' party.
38835.m: The SVP's party colour is green.

38836.q: Which picture can be seen in the SVP's logo?
38836.e: The SVP's logo shows a yellow sun on a green background.
38836.m: A yellow sun shines in the SVP's logo.

38837.q: Who elects the president of the SVP Switzerland?
38837.e: Parties elect their leaders themselves. In 2024, the SVP delegates elected Marcel Dettling as president.
38837.m: A party elects its president itself.

38838.q: Which two SVP members sit on the Federal Council (as of 2025)?
38838.e: Guy Parmelin has been on the Federal Council since 2016, Albert Rösti since 2023. Ueli Maurer stepped down at the end of 2022.
38838.m: The SVP is represented on the Federal Council by Guy Parmelin and Albert Rösti.

38839.q: What does the abbreviation SVP stand for?
38839.e: SVP stands for Schweizerische Volkspartei, the Swiss People's Party. For many years it has been the strongest party in the National Council.

38840.q: What is the SVP's position on Switzerland joining the European Union?
a: It demands joining the EU quickly
It wants a vote on joining every year
It has no position on it
38840.e: In its programme, the SVP stands up for an independent Switzerland and fights against joining the EU.
38840.m: The SVP is against Switzerland joining the EU.

38841.q: What did the SVP's deportation initiative, accepted in 2010, call for?
a: Foreigners who commit serious crimes should leave the country
38841.e: The deportation initiative demanded that foreigners be expelled after certain serious crimes. The people and the cantons accepted it in 2010.
38841.m: The SVP's deportation initiative was accepted in 2010.

38842.q: Where does the SP stand on the political spectrum?
38842.e: The SP stands up, for example, for social security and for employees. It is seen as a left-wing party. In 1943, Ernst Nobs became the first Social Democrat on the Federal Council.
38842.m: The SP is a left-wing party.

38843.q: Who was the first SP woman on the Federal Council?
38843.e: Ruth Dreifuss was elected in March 1993. Christiane Brunner had been the official candidate before, but was not elected.
38843.m: In 1993, Ruth Dreifuss became the first SP woman on the Federal Council.

38844.q: What does it mean that the SP has co-presidents?
a: Two people lead the party together
The Federal Council leads the party
38844.e: Since 2020, Mattea Meyer and Cédric Wermuth have led the SP Switzerland together. Co-presidents share the leadership.
38844.m: With co-presidents, two people lead together.

38845.q: In which event of 1918 did the SP and the trade unions play a leading role?
a: The founding of the Red Cross
The building of the Gotthard Tunnel
38845.e: The SP and the Swiss Trade Union Federation organised the national general strike in November 1918. Many of its demands were later put into practice.
38845.m: The 1918 general strike was backed by the SP and the trade unions.

38846.q: Which colour stands for the SP?
38846.e: Since the 19th century, red has been the colour of the labour movement and so also of the SP.
38846.m: The SP's party colour is red.

38847.q: Which two SP members sit on the Federal Council (as of 2025)?
38847.e: Elisabeth Baume-Schneider has been on the Federal Council since 2023, Beat Jans since 2024 as Alain Berset's successor.
38847.m: The SP is represented on the Federal Council by Elisabeth Baume-Schneider and Beat Jans.

38848.q: What is the SP called in French-speaking Switzerland?
38848.e: In French, the party is called “Parti socialiste suisse”, PS for short.
38848.m: In French, the SP is called Parti socialiste.

38849.q: What did the SP's premium relief initiative, voted on in 2024, want?
a: To limit health insurance premiums for households
38849.e: The initiative wanted nobody to have to pay more than 10 per cent of their income on health insurance premiums. It was rejected.
38849.m: The SP's premium relief initiative was voted on in 2024.

38850.q: What is the party called that was formed in 2009 from the merger of the FDP with the Liberal Party?
38850.e: The Radicals and the Liberals merged on 1 January 2009. The new party is called FDP.The Liberals.
38850.m: Since 2009, the party has been called FDP.The Liberals.

38851.q: Which value is especially important to the FDP?
38851.e: The FDP is a liberal party. It stands up for freedom, personal responsibility and a strong economy.
38851.m: The FDP is a liberal party that stresses freedom.

38852.q: Which political movement provided all members of the Federal Council from 1848 to 1891?
38852.e: The Radicals had built the federal state in 1848 and held all seven Federal Council seats until 1891.
38852.m: Until 1891, all Federal Councillors came from the Radicals.

38853.q: Which colour does the FDP use as its party colour?
38853.e: The FDP uses blue in its logo and campaigns.
38853.m: The FDP's party colour is blue.

38854.q: Which two FDP members sit on the Federal Council (as of 2025)?
38854.e: Ignazio Cassis has been on the Federal Council since 2017, Karin Keller-Sutter since 2019.
38854.m: The FDP is represented on the Federal Council by Ignazio Cassis and Karin Keller-Sutter.

38855.q: What is the French abbreviation for the FDP?
38855.e: PLR stands for “Parti libéral-radical”, the French name of FDP.The Liberals.
38855.m: In French-speaking Switzerland, the FDP is called PLR.

38856.q: Who leads a party such as the FDP Switzerland?
38856.e: Every party elects a president. The presidency leads the party and represents it in public.
38856.m: A party is led by its presidency.

38857.q: In which part of the country was the Liberal Party of Switzerland mainly strong before merging with the FDP?
38857.e: The Liberal Party was mainly rooted in Geneva, Vaud and Neuchâtel, as well as in Basel-Stadt. In 2009, it merged with the FDP.
38857.m: The Liberal Party was mainly strong in French-speaking Switzerland.

38858.q: Which colour does the Centre have in its logo?
38858.e: The Centre uses orange as its party colour, as the former CVP did.
38858.m: The Centre's party colour is orange.

38859.q: Which party used to be called the CVP?
38859.e: The CVP merged with the BDP in 2021. The new party is called the Centre (Die Mitte).
38859.m: The former CVP is now called the Centre.

38860.q: How many seats does the Centre have on the Federal Council (as of 2026)?
38860.e: The Centre is represented on the Federal Council by Martin Pfister. The other six seats belong to the SVP, SP and FDP.
38860.m: The Centre has one seat on the Federal Council.

38861.q: Which member of the Centre was elected to the Federal Council in 2025?
38861.e: Martin Pfister from the canton of Zug was elected in March 2025 as Viola Amherd's successor.
38861.m: Martin Pfister has represented the Centre on the Federal Council since 2025.

38862.q: Which party broke away from the SVP in 2008 and later became part of the Centre?
38862.e: The Conservative Democratic Party (BDP) was formed in 2008, mainly from SVP cantonal parties in the Grisons, Bern and Glarus.
38862.m: The BDP broke away from the SVP in 2008.

38863.q: What was the party called from 1970 to 2020, before it took the name “the Centre”?
38863.e: From 1970, the party was called the Christian Democratic People's Party, CVP for short. This name ended at the end of 2020.
38863.m: The Centre used to be called the Christian Democratic People's Party.

38864.q: What is the Centre called in French?
38864.e: In French, the party is called “Le Centre”, in Italian “Alleanza del Centro”.
38864.m: In French-speaking Switzerland, the Centre is called Le Centre.

38866.q: Which movement did the Green Party grow out of?
38866.e: In the 1970s and 1980s, many people wanted to protect nature better. The Green Party grew out of this environmental movement.
38866.m: The Greens grew out of the environmental movement.

38867.q: What is the Greens' youth party called?
38867.e: The Young Greens are the youth party of the Greens. For example, they launched the environmental responsibility initiative.
38867.m: The Greens' youth party is called the Young Greens.

38868.q: Which way of generating electricity have the Greens rejected since they were founded?
38868.e: The Greens rely on renewable energy such as sun, wind and water. They reject nuclear power stations because of the dangers and the radioactive waste.
38868.m: The Greens are against nuclear power stations.

38869.q: Which means of transport do the Greens especially want to promote?
38869.e: Trains, trams and buses use less energy per person than cars or aeroplanes. That is why the Greens want to expand public transport.

38870.q: Which party do the Greens often work with in parliament?
38870.e: The Greens and the SP are both on the political left and often have similar aims, for example on climate protection or social issues.
38870.m: The Greens often work together with the SP.

38871.q: What was the big success of the Greens and Green Liberals in the 2019 elections often called?
38871.e: In 2019, climate protection was a main topic, and both green parties made big gains. That is why the media spoke of a green wave.
38871.m: The 2019 elections went down in history as the green wave.

38872.q: Which issue is at the heart of the Greens’ politics?
a: Protecting the environment and the climate
38872.e: The Greens grew out of the environmental movement. Climate, nature and public transport are their core issues.
38872.m: The Greens campaign above all for the environment and the climate.

38873.q: Are the Greens represented in the Federal Council (as of 2025)?
38873.e: The Greens have stood for the Federal Council several times but were never elected. They are the largest party without a seat in the Federal Council.
38873.m: The Greens have never had a seat in the Federal Council.

38874.q: Roughly where does the Green Liberal Party stand politically?
38874.e: The GLP combines environmental protection with a liberal economic policy. That is why it is counted among the centre parties.
38874.m: The GLP is a centre party.

38875.q: Which party did the founders of the Green Liberals split from?
38875.e: The founders left the Greens because they felt the party was too far to the left.
38875.m: The Green Liberals split off from the Greens.

38876.q: What mainly sets the Green Liberals apart from the Greens?
a: They want to abolish the cantons
38876.e: Both parties want to protect the environment and the climate. The Green Liberals rely more on the market economy and less on bans.
38876.m: The GLP is green and business-friendly.

38877.q: Is the Green Liberal Party represented in the Federal Council (as of 2025)?
38877.e: The GLP is a fairly young party. It has never had a seat in the Federal Council so far.
38877.m: The GLP has no seat in the Federal Council.

38878.q: What does the Green Liberal Party combine in its programme?
a: Environmental protection and liberal economic policy
38878.e: The GLP wants to protect the environment and the climate, but relies on the market economy and personal responsibility to do so.
38878.m: The GLP combines environmental protection with a liberal economy.

38879.q: What is the GLP’s position on Switzerland’s relations with the EU?
a: It wants to cancel all treaties
It has no position on this
38879.e: The Green Liberals are seen as pro-European and support close cooperation with the EU.
38879.m: The GLP is in favour of close relations with the EU.

38880.q: Which colour dominates the Green Liberals’ logo?
38880.e: The GLP uses a light green, together with a light blue.
38880.m: The Green Liberals present themselves in light green.

38882.q: What does the abbreviation EVP stand for?
38882.e: EVP stands for the Evangelical People’s Party of Switzerland. It is a small party with Christian values.

38883.q: Is the EVP represented in the Federal Council (as of 2026)?
a: No, it is too small for that
Yes, it always provides the President of the Confederation
38883.e: The Federal Council is made up of members of the large parties. The EVP has only a few seats in parliament and no seat in the Federal Council.
38883.m: The EVP is a small party without a seat in the Federal Council.

38884.q: Which values does the EVP base its politics on?
38884.e: The EVP is guided by the Gospel and by Christian values such as love of one’s neighbour and responsibility.
38884.m: The EVP bases its politics on Christian values.

38885.q: Which religion does the word “evangelical” in the EVP’s name refer to?
38885.e: In German, “evangelisch” is the word for Protestant Christians. The EVP bases its politics on Christian values.
38885.m: The EVP is a party with Christian values.

38886.q: Why does the EVP not form its own parliamentary group in the Federal Parliament?
a: It does not want to vote
It only sits in the Council of States
38886.e: A parliamentary group needs at least five members. The EVP has fewer, so it joins a larger group.
38886.m: Small parties join larger groups in parliament.

38887.q: What is the EVP called in French?
38887.e: The French name is “Parti évangélique suisse”, abbreviated to PEV.
38887.m: In French, the EVP is called Parti évangélique suisse.

38888.q: What is the EVP’s youth party called?
38888.e: The Young EVP, jevp for short, has existed since 2004.
38888.m: The EVP’s youth party is called jevp.

38889.q: How is the EVP usually classified on social questions such as marriage and family?
38889.e: On the environment and social issues the EVP stands slightly left of centre, but on family and social questions it is rather conservative in its values.
38889.m: On social questions, the EVP is rather conservative in its values.

38890.q: Which body usually adopts the party programme in Swiss parties?
38890.e: In the delegates’ assembly, representatives of the cantonal parties vote on the programme.
38890.m: A party’s delegates decide on its programme.

38891.q: What is a programme called that sets out a party’s goals for one particular term of office only?
38891.e: An election manifesto names the goals for the next four years. It builds on the party’s long-term core values.
38891.m: For one legislative term, a party presents an election manifesto.

38892.q: What is a programme called that sets out a party’s long-term core values?
38892.e: A statement of principles applies for many years and describes what a party fundamentally stands for.
38892.m: A party’s core values are written in its statement of principles.

38893.q: What do a party’s statutes set out?
a: Its goals for the next election
The salaries of the Federal Councillors
38893.e: The statutes set out who can be a member, which bodies there are and how elections work. The political goals, on the other hand, are in the programme.
38893.m: The statutes decide how a party is organised.

38894.q: What is a paper called in which a party explains its view on one single issue?
38894.e: In a position paper, a party explains in detail what it wants, for example in energy or education policy.
38894.m: A position paper shows a party’s view on one issue.

38895.q: What is an issue called that a party is especially strongly linked with?
38895.e: Every party has a few core issues that are at the front of its programme, for example the environment for the Greens.
38895.m: A core issue is right at the front of a party’s programme.

38896.q: How can party members have a say in a new party programme?
a: They must launch a popular initiative
They write to the Federal Council
38896.e: Before the delegates vote, members and cantonal parties can submit proposals to change the draft.
38896.m: Members can help shape a party programme with proposals.

38897.q: Why is a party programme especially useful for voters?
a: To fill in their tax return
38897.e: Anyone who reads the programmes can see which goals the parties are pursuing and compare them with their own views.
38897.m: Party programmes let you compare the parties’ goals.

38898.q: What is the job of a party’s presidency?
a: It leads the party and represents it to the public
It chairs the meetings of the National Council
38898.e: The party president leads the party, plans its goals with the party leadership and explains the party’s position in public.
38898.m: The party presidency leads the party.

38899.q: Where do party presidents often explain their party’s opinion?
a: In the media, for example on television
Only in the Federal Supreme Court
38899.e: Party presidents give interviews, write articles and take part in debates on television. That is how voters find out what a party stands for.
38899.m: Party presidents represent their party in the media.

38900.q: Are party presidents allowed to sit in the Federal Parliament at the same time?
a: Yes, many are also members of parliament
Only if the Federal Council agrees
Only in the canton of Bern
38900.e: Many party presidents are also members of the National Council or the Council of States. That way they can also represent the party directly in parliament.
38900.m: Many party presidents also sit in parliament.

38901.q: What happens when a party president resigns?
a: The Federal Council appoints a successor
The Federal Supreme Court takes over the party
38901.e: When a president resigns, the party looks for candidates. The delegates’ assembly then elects the new party leadership.
38901.m: After a resignation, the party elects a new presidency.

38902.q: What is the person who leads a party called?
38902.e: A party is headed by its party presidency. The President of the Confederation, on the other hand, chairs the Federal Council, and a mayor leads a municipality.
38902.m: A party is led by a party presidency.

38903.q: Who often helps the party presidency lead the party?
38903.e: Besides the president, the party leadership usually includes several vice-presidents. There is also the general secretariat, which handles the daily work.
38903.m: Vice-presidents help to lead a party.

38904.q: In the large Swiss parties, who normally elects the party presidency?
a: The people at the ballot box
38904.e: The delegates from the cantonal parties elect the party leadership at a delegates’ assembly.
38904.m: The party presidency is elected by the delegates.

38905.q: What does it mean when a party is led by a co-presidency?
a: The Federal Council leads the party
38905.e: In a co-presidency, usually two people lead the party as equals and share the work.
38905.m: In a co-presidency, several people lead a party together.

38906.q: What is the office called that organises a party’s daily work?
38906.e: The general secretariat supports the presidency, plans campaigns and organises the party’s work.
38906.m: The general secretariat is a party’s central office.

38907.q: Which country does the division of politics into left and right come from?
38907.e: The terms arose in 1789 in the French National Assembly.
38907.m: The terms left and right come from France.

38908.q: Where do the terms left and right in politics originally come from?
a: From the seating plan in parliament
From the hand used to vote
38908.e: Seen from the president’s seat, the supporters of change sat on the left and the supporters of the king on the right.
38908.m: Left and right originally described seats in parliament.

38909.q: Which Federal Council party stands furthest to the left on the left-right scale?
38909.e: The SP campaigns strongly for the welfare state and redistribution, so it stands furthest to the left of the four Federal Council parties.
38909.m: Of the Federal Council parties, the SP stands furthest to the left.

38910.q: Which Federal Council party stands furthest to the right on the left-right scale?
38910.e: The SVP holds national conservative positions and stands furthest to the right of the Federal Council parties.
38910.m: Of the Federal Council parties, the SVP stands furthest to the right.

38911.q: What is a typical aim of left-wing parties?
38911.e: Left-wing parties want to reduce the gap between rich and poor, for example through social benefits and taxes.
38911.m: Left-wing parties call for more redistribution.

38912.q: What is a typical economic aim of parties to the right of centre?
38912.e: Parties to the right of centre want the state to hold back and the economy to act as freely as possible.
38912.m: Right-wing parties usually want less state and lower taxes.

38913.q: In Switzerland, what are the SVP, FDP and the Centre often called together?
38913.e: The SVP, FDP and the Centre are called bourgeois parties, as opposed to the SP and the Greens.
38913.m: The SVP, FDP and the Centre count as bourgeois parties.

38914.q: Which second axis is often added to the left-right scale to place parties more precisely?
38914.e: A party can be right-wing on the economy but socially liberal. That is why a second axis between liberal and conservative is often drawn.
38914.m: Besides left and right, people often distinguish between liberal and conservative.

38915.q: Where are the Green Liberals usually placed on the left-right scale?
38915.e: On environmental issues the GLP is close to the Greens, on economic issues close to the FDP. That is why it counts as a centre party.
38915.m: The Green Liberals stand in the centre of the left-right scale.

38916.q: What is the youth party of the Centre called?
38916.e: When the parent party was renamed, the Young CVP became the Young Centre.
38916.m: The youth party of the Centre is called the Young Centre.

38917.q: What is the FDP’s youth party called?
38917.e: The Young Liberals of Switzerland work closely with the FDP and have a seat on its executive board.
38917.m: The FDP’s youth party is called the Young Liberals.

38918.q: Which parent party does the JUSO belong to?
38918.e: JUSO stands for Young Socialists. It is the youth party of the SP Switzerland, but often acts independently.
38918.m: The JUSO is the youth party of the SP.

38919.q: What is the SVP’s youth party called?
38919.e: The Young SVP, JSVP for short, is the youth party of the Swiss People’s Party.
38919.m: The SVP’s youth party is called the Young SVP.

38920.q: What did the Young Liberals’ pensions initiative, voted on in 2024, call for?
a: A retirement age linked to life expectancy
38920.e: The initiative wanted to raise the retirement age first to 66 and then link it to life expectancy. It was rejected.
38920.m: The pensions initiative wanted to link the retirement age to life expectancy.

38921.q: Which youth party launched the environmental responsibility initiative, voted on in 2025?
38921.e: The initiative wanted Switzerland’s economy to stay within planetary boundaries. The people and the cantons rejected it in February 2025.
38921.m: The environmental responsibility initiative came from the Young Greens.

38922.q: What did the JUSO’s 99% initiative of 2021 call for?
a: Taxing income from capital more heavily
38922.e: Income from capital such as interest and dividends above a tax-free allowance was to be taxed at 1.5 times the rate. The initiative was rejected in September 2021.
38922.m: The 99% initiative wanted to tax income from capital more heavily.

a: A party of young people that belongs to a larger party
A party only for children under 10
A party that was only founded last year
38923.e: Youth parties such as the JUSO or the Young Liberals are parties of young people. They belong to a parent party but often have their own, sometimes more radical, ideas.
38923.m: A youth party is the party of the young members of a larger party.

38924.q: Which JUSO initiative wanted the highest salary in a company to be no more than twelve times the lowest?
38924.e: The 1:12 initiative was clearly rejected by the people and the cantons in 2013.
38924.m: The 1:12 initiative wanted to limit very high managers’ salaries.

38925.q: Which parties have to disclose their funding to the Confederation?
a: Parties represented in the Federal Assembly
Only the parties in the Federal Council
All clubs and associations in Switzerland
38925.e: The rule applies to all political parties with at least one seat in the National Council or the Council of States.
38925.m: Parties in the federal parliament must disclose their funding.

38926.q: How often do parties have to report their income and large donations to the Confederation?
38926.e: The parties submit their details every year. They are then published on the internet.
38926.m: Parties disclose their finances every year.

38927.q: What did the transparency initiative call for?
a: Parties should show where their money comes from
38927.e: The initiative wanted parties and campaigns to disclose who donates large amounts to them. Parliament met many of its demands with a counter-proposal, so it was withdrawn.
38927.m: The transparency initiative wanted to reveal where parties get their money.

38928.q: Why should parties disclose where their money comes from?
a: So that people can see who supports them
So that they pay less tax
So that they get more members
So that the Federal Council can lead them
38928.e: If you know who supports a party with a lot of money, you can form your own opinion better. The rules for this are in the Federal Act on Political Rights.
38928.m: Transparency shows who supports parties with money.

a: Money that someone gives to a party as a gift
A tax that everyone has to pay
38929.e: Donations are voluntary gifts of money from private individuals or companies. Today, parties have to disclose large donations.
38929.m: A party donation is a voluntary gift of money to a party.

38930.q: What does the word transparency mean when it comes to party funding?
a: Openness, everyone can look it up
38930.e: Transparent means see-through. In political funding it means that it is public where the parties’ money comes from.

38931.q: What can private individuals do with donations to a party on their tax return?
a: Deduct them up to a maximum amount
Give them back to the Federal Council
38931.e: Since 2011, membership fees and donations to parties can be deducted from taxable income up to a maximum amount. In this way the state wants to encourage donations.
38931.m: Party donations can be deducted from tax up to a maximum amount.

38932.q: What amount do party members pay to their party regularly?
38932.e: Members pay a fee every year. Together with donations and contributions from elected officials, it funds the party.
38932.m: With their membership fee, members support their party.

38933.q: How are the parties in Switzerland mainly funded at federal level?
a: From the profits of the National Bank
38933.e: Switzerland has no direct state funding of parties. Only the parliamentary groups receive contributions for their work.
38933.m: Swiss parties live mainly on private money.

38934.q: What is the abbreviation for the canton of the Grisons?
38934.e: The abbreviation GR comes from the German name “Graubünden”. It appears, for example, on car number plates from this canton.
38934.m: The Grisons has the abbreviation GR.

38935.q: Which canton does the abbreviation NW belong to?
38935.e: NW stands for Nidwalden in Central Switzerland. Neuchâtel has the abbreviation NE.
38935.m: NW is the abbreviation for Nidwalden.

38936.q: Which abbreviation does the canton of Valais have?
38936.e: The abbreviation VS comes from the French name “Valais”. The canton is bilingual, French and German.
38936.m: Valais has the abbreviation VS, after its French name.

38937.q: Which canton has the abbreviation VD?
38937.e: VD stands for “Vaud”, the French name of the canton. Its capital is Lausanne.
38937.m: VD is the abbreviation for the canton of Vaud.

38938.q: Which canton has the abbreviation TI?
38938.e: TI comes from “Ticino”, the Italian name of the canton. Thurgau has the abbreviation TG.

38939.q: Which canton has the abbreviation AR?
38939.e: AR stands for Appenzell Ausserrhoden. Appenzell Innerrhoden has AI and Aargau AG.
38939.m: AR is the abbreviation for Appenzell Ausserrhoden.

38940.q: How many cantons have only half a cantonal vote in popular votes?
38940.e: Obwalden, Nidwalden, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden each have half a cantonal vote. They used to be called half-cantons.
38940.m: Six cantons have only half a cantonal vote.

38941.q: Which canton has the largest area?
38941.e: With just over 7,100 square kilometres, the Grisons is the largest canton. It is larger than Valais and Bern.
38941.m: The Grisons is the largest Swiss canton by area.

38942.q: Which canton has the smallest area?
38942.e: Basel-Stadt covers only about 37 square kilometres. Besides the city of Basel, only Riehen and Bettingen belong to it.
38942.m: Basel-Stadt is the smallest canton by area.

38943.q: What does every canton have, just like Switzerland as a whole?
38943.e: Every canton has its own constitution. However, it must not contradict the Federal Constitution.
38943.m: Every canton has its own constitution.

38944.q: According to the Federal Constitution, who must approve a cantonal constitution?
38944.e: Article 51 of the Federal Constitution requires the people to approve the cantonal constitution. A constitution without a popular vote would not be valid.
38944.m: A cantonal constitution needs the approval of the voters.

38945.q: What applies if cantonal law contradicts federal law?
38945.e: Article 49 of the Federal Constitution says that federal law takes precedence over conflicting cantonal law. This is called the primacy of federal law.

38947.q: Which law is the most important in a canton and stands above all others?
38947.e: The cantonal constitution is the basic law of a canton. All other cantonal laws must fit in with it.
38947.m: The cantonal constitution is a canton’s most important law.

38949.q: Who must agree if a cantonal constitution is to be changed?
38949.e: A cantonal constitution can be changed. Because it is the canton’s most important law, the people must vote on it.
38949.m: The people vote on any change to the cantonal constitution.

38950.q: What is the capital of the canton of the Grisons?
38950.e: Chur is the capital of the Grisons and is considered one of the oldest towns in Switzerland. Davos is well known, but it is not the capital.
38950.m: Chur is the capital of the Grisons.

38951.q: What is the capital of the canton of Valais called in German?
38951.e: The capital of Valais is called Sion in French and Sitten in German. It lies in the French-speaking part of the canton.
38951.m: Sion, Sitten in German, is the capital of Valais.

38952.q: What is the capital of the canton of Basel-Landschaft?
38952.e: Liestal is the capital of Basel-Landschaft. Allschwil has more inhabitants, but it is not the capital.
38952.m: Liestal is the capital of Basel-Landschaft.

38953.q: What is the capital of the canton of Nidwalden?
38953.e: Stans is the capital of Nidwalden. Sarnen is the capital of the neighbouring canton of Obwalden.
38953.m: Stans is the capital of Nidwalden.

38954.q: Which town is the capital of the canton of Ticino?
38954.e: Bellinzona is the capital of Ticino and is famous for its three castles. Lugano is the largest town in the canton.
38954.m: Bellinzona is the capital of Ticino, although Lugano is larger.

38955.q: What is the role of the cantonal government (Regierungsrat) in a canton?
38955.e: The cantonal government is the canton’s executive. It runs the administration and puts the laws into practice.
38955.m: The Regierungsrat is a canton’s government.

38956.q: How many members does a cantonal government almost always have?
38956.e: Most cantonal governments have five or seven members. An odd number prevents ties in votes.
38956.m: Cantonal governments usually have five or seven members.

38957.q: What is the cantonal government called in Geneva and Vaud?
38957.e: In French it is called “Conseil d’État”, the Council of State. Valais, Fribourg and Ticino also speak of the Council of State.
38957.m: In French-speaking Switzerland, the cantonal government is called the Council of State.

38958.q: What is the principle called by which a cantonal government defends its decisions together in public?
38958.e: Under the collegiality principle, all members support a government decision, even if they were against it. The same applies to the Federal Council.
38958.m: Under the collegiality principle, the whole government stands behind its decisions.

38959.q: Which electoral system is used to elect the cantonal government in most cantons?
38959.e: In the majority system, the people with the most votes are elected. Only a few cantons, such as Ticino, elect their government by proportional representation.
38959.m: Most cantonal governments are elected by the majority system.

38960.q: How many members does the government of the canton of Lucerne have?
38960.e: The government of the canton of Lucerne has five members. Each one heads one of the five departments.
38960.m: The Lucerne government has five members.

38961.q: What is the parliament of the canton of Zurich called?
38961.e: The Zurich parliament is called the Kantonsrat (Cantonal Council). Other cantons call their parliament the Grosser Rat or the Landrat.
38961.m: In the canton of Zurich, the parliament is called the Kantonsrat.

38962.q: What is the parliament of the canton of Basel-Landschaft called?
38962.e: In Basel-Landschaft, the cantonal parliament is called the Landrat. Uri, Glarus and Nidwalden also use this name for their parliament.
38962.m: Basel-Landschaft calls its cantonal parliament the Landrat.

38963.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the cantonal parliament of Ticino?
38963.e: Ticino is the Italian-speaking canton of Switzerland. That is why Italian is spoken in its cantonal parliament, the Gran Consiglio, too.
38963.m: In the Ticino cantonal parliament, people speak Italian.

38965.q: Which system is mostly used to elect the cantonal parliaments?
38965.e: In a proportional election, parties receive seats in proportion to their votes. That way smaller parties are represented in parliament too.
38965.m: Cantonal parliaments are mostly elected by the proportional system.

38966.e: The government draws up the budget, and parliament decides on it. In this way parliament controls the canton’s finances.
38966.m: The cantonal parliament decides on the canton’s budget.

38967.q: Which branch of state power does a cantonal parliament belong to?
38967.e: Parliament makes the laws and therefore belongs to the legislative branch. The government and the courts form the other two branches.
38967.m: The cantonal parliament is the law-making power, the legislative.

38968.q: Which language is spoken in the parliament of the canton of Jura?
38968.e: The canton of Jura is French-speaking. Its cantonal parliament is therefore simply called “Parlement” in French.
38968.m: In the parliament of the canton of Jura, people speak French.

38969.q: In which canton is a Landsgemeinde still held every year today?
38969.e: Today there is a Landsgemeinde only in Glarus and in Appenzell Innerrhoden. There, people vote in the open air.

38970.q: What form of democracy is a Landsgemeinde?
38970.e: At the Landsgemeinde, the voters gather and decide for themselves. It is the oldest form of direct democracy in Switzerland.
38970.m: The Landsgemeinde is an assembly democracy.

38971.q: How do people vote at a Landsgemeinde?
38971.e: At the Landsgemeinde, the voters stand in a ring and raise their hand, often holding their voting card.
38971.m: At the Landsgemeinde, people vote by raising their hands.

38972.q: Which tax is levied only by the cantons and municipalities, but not by the Confederation?
38972.e: Wealth tax is a matter for the cantons and municipalities. The Confederation does not tax the wealth of private individuals.
38972.m: Wealth tax is levied only by the cantons and municipalities.

38973.q: What is it called when cantons try to attract companies and residents with low taxes?
38973.e: Because each canton sets its own tax rates, the cantons compete with each other. This tax competition is a result of federalism.
38973.m: Different cantonal taxes lead to tax competition.

38974.q: What does it mean that the cantons have their own taxing power?
a: They may levy their own taxes and set the amount themselves
They do not have to collect any taxes
They may only levy dog taxes
38974.e: The cantons may levy their own taxes and decide the tax rates themselves. A federal law only harmonises the rules, not the level of the taxes.
38974.m: The cantons decide the level of their taxes themselves.

38975.q: In which canton do you pay income tax if you move house during the year?
a: In the canton you live in at the end of the year
In the canton where you were born
In the canton you lived in at the start of the year
38975.e: What counts is where you live at the end of the tax period, that is on 31 December. This canton taxes the whole year’s income.
38975.m: If you move, you pay income tax in the canton you live in at the end of the year.

38976.q: Who is responsible for inheritance tax in Switzerland?
38976.e: There is no federal inheritance tax. Each canton decides for itself whether inheritance tax is charged and how much.
38976.m: Inheritance tax is a matter for the cantons.

38977.q: Which tax may only the Confederation levy?
38977.e: According to the Federal Constitution, VAT is a federal tax. The cantons may not levy a similar tax.
38977.m: VAT is purely a federal tax.

38978.q: Who is mainly responsible for compulsory schooling in Switzerland?
38978.e: According to Article 62 of the Federal Constitution, schooling is a matter for the cantons. That is why there are differences from canton to canton.
38978.m: The cantons are responsible for state schools.

38979.q: What is the joint curriculum of the German-speaking Swiss cantons called?
38979.e: Lehrplan 21 applies in the 21 German-speaking and multilingual cantons. The cantons developed it together.

38980.q: How many years does compulsory schooling last in most cantons, including kindergarten?
38980.e: Compulsory schooling includes two years of kindergarten, six years of primary school and three years of lower secondary school. That makes eleven years.

38981.q: Since a popular vote in 1985, when does the school year begin in Switzerland?
38981.e: In 1985, the people approved a common start of the school year in late summer. Before that, the school year began in spring in several cantons.
38981.m: The school year begins in late summer throughout Switzerland.

38982.q: What is the joint curriculum of the French-speaking cantons called?
38982.e: French-speaking Switzerland has the Plan d’études romand (PER). In German-speaking Switzerland, Lehrplan 21 applies.
38982.m: French-speaking Switzerland works with the Plan d’études romand.

38983.q: Under HarmoS, at what age does compulsory schooling begin with kindergarten?
38983.e: In the HarmoS cantons, children must go to kindergarten from the age of 4. Kindergarten counts as part of compulsory schooling.
38983.m: Under HarmoS, compulsory schooling begins at 4.

38984.q: How many years does compulsory schooling last under HarmoS, counting kindergarten?
38984.e: Under HarmoS, compulsory schooling lasts 11 years: 2 years of kindergarten, 6 years of primary school and 3 years of lower secondary school.
38984.m: Under HarmoS, compulsory schooling lasts 11 years.

38985.q: Besides fixed school hours, what must HarmoS cantons offer?
38985.e: The cantons that have joined commit themselves to fixed school hours and to offering day care, for example lunch clubs and supervision. Using them is voluntary.
38985.m: HarmoS requires fixed school hours and day care facilities.

38986.q: What is the purpose of fiscal equalisation between the cantons?
a: Rich cantons and the Confederation support poorer cantons
All cantons pay the same amount to the army
The cantons share their money with municipalities abroad
The Confederation takes all taxes away from the cantons
38986.e: Fiscal equalisation makes sure that all cantons have enough money for their tasks. It was reorganised with the NFA.
38986.m: Fiscal equalisation helps financially weak cantons.

38987.q: What are cantons called that pay into fiscal equalisation?
38987.e: Financially strong cantons such as Zug or Zurich pay in and are called donor cantons. The others receive money and are called recipient cantons.
38987.m: Donor cantons pay into fiscal equalisation.

38988.q: What are cantons called that receive money from fiscal equalisation?
38988.e: Cantons with low tax revenue, for example Uri or Jura, receive money from fiscal equalisation. They are called recipient cantons.
38988.m: Recipient cantons receive money from fiscal equalisation.

38989.q: Why do some cantons have less tax revenue than others?
a: Because there are fewer companies and high earners there
Because they are not allowed to levy taxes
Because the Federal Council decides so
38989.e: Cantons with little economic strength collect less tax. The resource equalisation therefore gives them extra money.
38989.m: Economically weak cantons receive money from fiscal equalisation.

38990.q: Why do mountain cantons receive money from fiscal equalisation?
a: Roads and services in the mountains cost more
Because they are the oldest cantons
38990.e: Steep terrain, long distances and few inhabitants make many tasks more expensive. The burden equalisation compensates for these costs.
38990.m: Mountain cantons receive money for their higher costs.

38991.q: Who pays for the NFA’s resource equalisation?
38991.e: The resource equalisation is funded jointly by the Confederation and the cantons with strong resources. The Confederation pays the larger share.
38991.m: The Confederation and financially strong cantons pay for the resource equalisation.

38992.q: Which of these cantons pays into the resource equalisation?
38992.e: Zug is one of the donor cantons, as are Zurich, Geneva, Schwyz, Nidwalden and Basel-Stadt. Uri, Jura and Valais receive money.
38992.m: Zug is one of the donor cantons in fiscal equalisation.

38993.q: Which of these cantons receives money from fiscal equalisation?
38993.e: Uri has low tax revenue and receives money. Zug, Zurich and Geneva are donor cantons.
38993.m: Uri receives money from fiscal equalisation.

38994.q: Which task did the Confederation take over completely from the cantons with the NFA?
38994.e: With the NFA, building, running and maintaining the national motorways became entirely a federal task. The aim was to make responsibilities clearer.
38994.m: Since the NFA, the national motorways are purely a federal matter.

38995.q: How many stars are on the coat of arms of the canton of Valais?
38995.e: The coat of arms of Valais is divided vertically into white and red and has 13 stars. They recall the old districts of Valais.
38995.m: The coat of arms of Valais has 13 stars.

38996.q: Which motto is on the coat of arms of the canton of Vaud?
38996.e: The green and white coat of arms of Vaud bears the words “Liberté et Patrie”, meaning “Freedom and Fatherland”. The motto dates from the time the canton was founded.
38996.m: The coat of arms of Vaud bears the motto Liberté et Patrie.

38997.q: Who is represented in the Conference of Cantonal Governments (KdK)?
a: All the members of the Council of States
38997.e: Each of the 26 cantonal governments has a seat in the KdK. That way the cantons can act together.
38997.m: All the cantonal governments are represented in the KdK.

38998.q: Why do the cantons act together in the Conference of Cantonal Governments?
a: Together they carry more weight with the Confederation
Because otherwise they may not make laws
Because the Federal Council orders it
38998.e: When all 26 cantons speak with one voice, the Confederation listens to them more. That is why the cantonal governments work together in the KdK.
38998.m: Together, the cantons carry more weight with the Confederation.

38999.q: In which city is the Conference of Cantonal Governments based?
38999.e: The KdK has its secretariat in the House of the Cantons in Bern, close to the Federal Palace.
38999.m: The KdK is based in Bern.

39000.q: What is a main aim of the Conference of Cantonal Governments?
a: To represent the cantons’ interests to the Confederation
39000.e: The KdK makes sure that the cantons represent their interests to the Confederation together. It also promotes cooperation between the cantons.
39000.m: The KdK represents the cantons’ interests to the Confederation.

39001.q: How many cantonal governments are represented in the Conference of Cantonal Governments?
39001.e: Switzerland has 26 cantons. Each cantonal government has a seat in the KdK.
39001.m: All 26 cantons are represented in the KdK.

39002.q: Which conference brings together the cantonal ministers of education?
a: The Conference of Cantonal Ministers of Education (EDK)
39002.e: In the EDK, the cantons work together on schools, for example on the curriculum. There are conferences like this for many areas.
39002.m: In the EDK, the cantons work together on education.

39003.q: What is a concordat in Swiss politics?
a: A ruling of the Federal Supreme Court
39003.e: A concordat is an agreement that two or more cantons make with each other. In this way they deal with shared tasks without the Confederation.
39003.m: A concordat is a treaty between cantons.

39004.q: What must cantons bear in mind with a concordat?
a: It must not contradict federal law
It must be approved by other countries
It may only apply for one year
39004.e: Cantons may make treaties with each other. However, these must not go against federal law.
39004.m: A concordat must not contradict federal law.

39005.q: Which problem is the so-called hooligan concordat aimed at?
39005.e: The concordat on measures against violence at sports events allows, for example, bans from certain areas. It is meant to prevent riots around football and ice hockey matches.
39005.m: The hooligan concordat fights violence at sports events.

39006.q: Why do cantons make a concordat?
a: To deal with a task together
39006.e: Some tasks are hard for one canton to manage alone, for example running prisons. With a concordat, cantons work together.
39006.m: With a concordat, cantons deal with tasks together.

a: Money to support someone’s education or training
39007.e: With a grant, the canton helps people who could otherwise hardly afford education or training. The cantons have common rules for this.
39007.m: A grant helps to pay for education or training.

39008.q: Who pays part of the costs when someone goes to university in another canton?
39008.e: Universities are expensive. That is why the canton of residence pays a contribution to the university in the other canton. The cantons have an agreement on this.
39008.m: The canton of residence contributes to the cost of studying.

39009.q: Who decides whether a canton joins a concordat?
39009.e: Each canton decides on joining according to its own law, often through parliament or in a popular vote. No canton can be forced to join.
39009.m: Each canton decides for itself whether to join a concordat.

a: Member states have their own powers
39010.e: In federalism, the state as a whole and its member states share power. In Switzerland, the cantons are the member states.
39010.m: In federalism, the member states have their own powers.

39011.q: Which municipality moved from the canton of Bern to the canton of Jura on 1 January 2026?
39011.e: In 2021, the voters of Moutier decided to move to the canton of Jura. The change of canton took place on 1 January 2026.
39011.m: Moutier has belonged to the canton of Jura since 2026.

39012.q: What is cooperation between the cantons without the Confederation called?
39012.e: When cantons work directly with each other, this is called horizontal federalism. Cooperation between the Confederation and the cantons is called vertical.
39012.m: Cooperation between cantons is called horizontal federalism.

39013.q: How do people vote in cantons without a Landsgemeinde?
a: By raising hands in the ring
39013.e: Most cantons have no Landsgemeinde. There, people vote at the ballot box or by post.
39013.m: Without a Landsgemeinde, people vote at the ballot box.

39014.q: What does the Glarus Landsgemeinde decide on, among other things?
39014.e: In Glarus, the Landsgemeinde is the highest body. It decides on changes to the constitution and laws and on major spending.
39014.m: In Glarus, the Landsgemeinde passes the cantonal laws.

39015.q: How many old leagues are united in the coat of arms of the Grisons?
39015.e: The coat of arms of the Grisons unites the emblems of the Grey League, the League of God’s House and the League of the Ten Jurisdictions. The canton grew out of these three leagues.
39015.m: The coat of arms of the Grisons recalls the three old leagues.

39016.q: How is the coat of arms of the canton of Zurich divided?
39016.e: The Zurich coat of arms is divided diagonally, white at the top and blue at the bottom. You can also see these colours on Zurich’s trams.
39016.m: The Zurich coat of arms is divided diagonally into white and blue.

39017.q: Which colours does the vertically divided coat of arms of the canton of Lucerne show?
39017.e: The Lucerne coat of arms is divided vertically, blue on the left and white on the right. It is one of the simplest cantonal coats of arms.
39017.m: The Lucerne coat of arms is blue and white.

39018.q: What does the coat of arms of the canton of Zug show?
39018.e: The Zug coat of arms is white with a blue horizontal band in the middle. White and blue are the cantonal colours of Zug.
39018.m: The Zug coat of arms shows a blue band on white.

39019.q: Which canton has the most inhabitants?
39019.e: More than 1.5 million people live in the canton of Zurich (as of 2024). This makes it clearly the most populous canton.
39019.m: Zurich is the most populous canton.

39020.q: Which canton has the abbreviation SZ?
39020.e: SZ stands for Schwyz. Solothurn has SO, Schaffhausen SH and St Gallen SG.
39020.m: SZ is the abbreviation for the canton of Schwyz.

39021.q: Which of these cantons is officially bilingual in German and French?
39021.e: In the canton of Fribourg, French and German are official languages. Bern and Valais are also bilingual.

39022.q: Which town is the capital of the canton of Vaud?
39022.e: Lausanne on Lake Geneva is the capital of Vaud. The Federal Supreme Court is also based there.
39022.m: Lausanne is the capital of the canton of Vaud.

39023.q: What is the capital of the canton of Aargau?
39023.e: Aarau is the capital of Aargau. In 1798 the town was briefly the first capital of the Helvetic Republic.
39023.m: Aarau is the capital of the canton of Aargau.

39024.q: According to the Federal Constitution, what kind of constitution must every canton have?
39024.e: Article 51 of the Federal Constitution says that every canton shall have a democratic constitution. So a canton may not have a king, for example.
39024.m: Every canton must have a democratic constitution.

39025.q: What is the tax called that companies pay on their profit?
39025.e: Companies pay a profit tax on their profit to the Confederation, the canton and the municipality. The cantons set their own rates.
39025.m: Companies pay profit tax on their profit.

39026.q: A plot of land was bought for 500,000 francs and later sold for 700,000 francs. On which amount is the property gains tax calculated?
39026.e: Only the gain is taxed, that is the difference between the selling price and the purchase price: 700,000 minus 500,000 makes 200,000 francs.
39026.m: Property gains tax is calculated only on the gain.

39027.q: According to the Federal Constitution, who must approve a change to the borders between cantons?
39027.e: Changes of territory between cantons need the approval of the population and cantons concerned. In addition, the Federal Assembly must approve them.
39027.m: Cantonal borders only change with the approval of the Federal Assembly.

39028.q: Which canton clearly rejected looking into a merger of the two Basels in 2014?
39028.e: In 2014, Basel-Stadt voted in favour of looking into a merger, but Basel-Landschaft clearly rejected it. That is why the two cantons remain separate.
39028.m: In 2014, Basel-Landschaft said no to looking into a merger with Basel-Stadt.

39029.q: What is the agreement called with which many cantons are making their state schools more alike?
39029.e: With the HarmoS concordat, many cantons have brought into line things such as the school starting age and the length of the school stages.
39029.m: HarmoS makes the cantons’ state schools more alike.

39030.e: In Switzerland, the cantons are responsible for schools. HarmoS is therefore an agreement between the cantons, a so-called concordat.
39030.m: HarmoS is an agreement between the cantons.

39031.q: What does the name HarmoS stand for?
39031.e: HarmoS is short for the Intercantonal Agreement on the Harmonisation of Compulsory Schooling. It brings key features of the schools into line.
39031.m: HarmoS stands for the harmonisation of compulsory schooling.

39033.q: What is the right of municipalities to manage many of their own affairs called?
39033.e: Autonomy means self-determination. The cantons decide how much the municipalities may decide for themselves.
39033.m: Thanks to municipal autonomy, municipalities decide many things themselves.

39034.q: Who decides how much the municipalities may decide for themselves?
39034.e: Municipalities belong to a canton. Each canton decides how much autonomy its municipalities have.
39034.m: The canton decides how independent its municipalities are.

39035.q: Which municipality has been the largest in Switzerland by area since 2015?
39035.e: Since 1 January 2015, Scuol in the Lower Engadine has been the largest municipality in Switzerland by area, at around 438 km².
39035.m: Scuol in the Grisons is the largest Swiss municipality by area.

39036.q: Which municipality has the most inhabitants?
39036.e: The city of Zurich is the most populous municipality in Switzerland. It is followed by Geneva and Basel.
39036.m: Zurich is the largest Swiss municipality by population.

39037.q: What often happens to very small municipalities in Switzerland?
a: They are sold to other countries
They get their own Federal Councillor
39037.e: Small municipalities often cannot find enough people for the official posts. That is why they merge with neighbouring municipalities.
39037.m: Small municipalities often merge with their neighbours.

39038.q: Which body is the legislature in most small municipalities?
39038.e: At the municipal assembly, voters can take part in decisions directly. It is the law-making body in small and medium-sized municipalities.
39038.m: In small municipalities, the municipal assembly decides directly.

39039.q: How do people usually vote at a municipal assembly?
39039.e: The voters raise their hands, and tellers count the votes. On request, there can also be a secret vote.
39039.m: At the municipal assembly, people usually vote openly with raised hands.

a: An election of the municipal council
39040.e: In a merger, two or more municipalities join together to form a new municipality. The old municipalities no longer exist afterwards.
39040.m: In a municipal merger, several municipalities become one.

39041.q: Why is the number of municipalities in Switzerland getting smaller and smaller?
39041.e: Around 1850 there were over 3,000 municipalities; today there are about 2,100. Many municipalities have merged.
39041.m: Because of mergers, there are fewer and fewer municipalities.

39042.q: What advantage do municipalities hope to gain from a merger?
a: To do their tasks better together
39042.e: A larger municipality can often run schools, administration and roads more cheaply. It also finds people for the official posts more easily.
39042.m: Mergers are meant to make municipalities stronger.

39044.q: Apart from the municipalities, who usually also has to approve a municipal merger?
39044.e: Municipalities belong to a canton. That is why the canton usually has to approve a merger.

39045.q: What changes for the inhabitants after a municipal merger?
a: They have a joint municipal council
They lose the right to vote
They all have to move house
39045.e: After the merger there is only one municipality with one joint authority. But people still live in the same place.
39045.m: After a merger, a joint municipal council governs.

39047.q: Which problem of small municipalities is often a reason for a merger?
a: Too few people for the official posts
39047.e: Small municipalities often cannot find enough people for the municipal council and other posts. Debts or high taxes can also lead to a merger.
39047.m: A lack of candidates for official posts encourages municipal mergers.

39048.q: What is the role of the municipal council (Gemeinderat) in most small Swiss municipalities?
39048.e: In most small municipalities, the municipal council is the executive. It runs the municipality and carries out the decisions.
39048.m: In small municipalities, the municipal council is the executive.

39049.q: How many members does a municipal council usually have?
39049.e: A municipal council usually has five to nine members. Each member is responsible for particular areas.
39049.m: A municipal council usually consists of five to nine people.

39050.q: In many municipalities, what is the member who leads the municipal council called?
39050.e: One member of the municipal council is the mayor. They chair the meetings and represent the municipality to the outside world.
39050.m: The mayor leads the municipal council.

39051.q: In some cantons, which other title is used for the head of a municipality?
39051.e: The title differs from canton to canton; in Aargau, for example, it is Gemeindeammann or Stadtammann. The job is the same as that of the mayor (Gemeindepräsident).
39051.m: In some cantons, the mayor is called the Gemeindeammann.

39052.q: What is the executive of the city of Zurich called?
39052.e: In the city of Zurich, the Stadtrat (city council) is the government. There, the Gemeinderat is the parliament.
39052.m: In the city of Zurich, the Stadtrat governs.

39053.q: What is the parliament of the city of Bern called?
39053.e: In the city of Bern, the government is called the Gemeinderat. The parliament, with 80 seats, is called the Stadtrat.
39053.m: In the city of Bern, the Stadtrat is the parliament.

39054.q: How do municipal councillors in small municipalities usually do their job?
39054.e: Municipal councillors in small municipalities usually work for the municipality alongside their job. This is called the militia system. In big cities the post is full-time.
39054.m: In the militia system, citizens take on public posts alongside their job.

39055.q: Who elects the municipal council in almost all Swiss municipalities?
39055.e: The municipality’s voters elect the members of the municipal council at the ballot box or at the municipal assembly.
39055.m: The people elect their municipal council themselves.

39056.q: Which system is mostly used to elect the municipal council?
39056.e: In a majority election, the people with the most votes are elected. Some towns, such as Bern or Biel, elect their executive by proportional representation.
39056.m: Municipal councils are mostly elected by majority vote.

39057.e: The Einwohnerrat is an elected parliament of a municipality. It is the legislature and decides on important matters.
39057.m: The Einwohnerrat is a municipality’s parliament.

39058.q: What does a municipal parliament replace?
39058.e: In municipalities with a parliament, elected representatives decide instead of all voters at an assembly. This is especially practical in larger municipalities.
39058.m: A municipal parliament replaces the municipal assembly.

39059.q: In municipalities without a parliament, where do the voters decide on important matters?
39059.e: Most Swiss municipalities have no parliament. There, the voters meet at the municipal assembly and decide directly.
39059.m: Without a municipal parliament, the municipal assembly decides.

39060.q: In which canton must every municipality have a parliament?
39060.e: In the cantons of Geneva and Neuchâtel, a municipal parliament is compulsory for all municipalities. Municipal parliaments are much more common in French-speaking Switzerland than in German-speaking Switzerland.
39060.m: In Geneva, every municipality has a parliament.

39061.q: Which system is used to elect most municipal parliaments?
39061.e: In a proportional election, parties receive seats in proportion to their votes. That way smaller parties are represented too.
39061.m: Municipal parliaments are mostly elected by proportional representation.

39062.q: What is the municipal parliament called in the canton of Neuchâtel?
39062.e: In the canton of Neuchâtel, the municipal parliament is called the Conseil général. The Conseil fédéral, on the other hand, is the Federal Council, and the Conseil d’État the cantonal government.
39062.m: In Neuchâtel, the municipal parliament is called the Conseil général.

39063.q: What can voters often use against a decision of the municipal parliament?
39063.e: Many decisions of municipal parliaments are subject to the optional referendum. With enough signatures, there is a popular vote.
39063.m: With the referendum, the people have the last word in the municipality too.

39064.q: In Basel-Stadt, which parliament is also the parliament of the city of Basel?
39064.e: Basel-Stadt has no separate city parliament. The cantonal Grand Council also takes on this task for the city of Basel.
39064.m: In Basel-Stadt, the Grand Council is also the city parliament.

39065.q: What is a municipality’s tax multiplier (Steuerfuss)?
a: A percentage of the basic tax
A measure of the municipality’s area
A tax office in the cellar
39065.e: The tax multiplier states what percentage of the basic tax you pay to the municipality. The basic tax comes from the cantonal tax scale.
39065.m: The tax multiplier decides how much municipal tax you pay.
